title: Typed logical-scalar versions of && and ||
motivation: `builtins.fir` had no version of `&&` or `||` for two unboxed logical scalars. So mandelbrot's loop condition boxed a logical, built an argument array, called the generic `&&` through `Fir_call_builtin`, and unboxed the result, on every trip of the inner loop.
solution: `builtins.fir` adds `&&` and `||` as `(lhs:L, rhs:L) --> L`, and `as.logical` as `(x:L, ddd:miss) --> L`. `runtime_inline.h` adds the three C helpers, with R's NA rules written out, because `NA_LOGICAL` is not 0 and C's `&&` would be wrong. The FIŘ interpreter (`Builtins.java`) registers the same signatures. `Unbox` then picks the typed versions without any Fir2C change, and mandelbrot's module calls no `Fir_call_builtin` any more.

files.client/rsh/src/fir2c/runtime_inline.h: Adds inline `&&` and `||` on two logical scalars with R's NA rules, and an `as.logical` of a logical scalar that returns it.
files.server/src/main/java/org/prlprg/fir/inte: Registers the interpreter versions `(L, L) --> L` of `&&` and `||` and `(L, miss) --> L` of `as.logical`.
files.server/src/main/resources/org/prlprg/fir: Adds the signatures `(lhs:L, rhs:L) --> L` to `&&` and `||`, and `(x:L, ddd:miss) --> L` to `as.logical`.
files.server/src/test/resources/org/prlprg/exa: New example that runs `&&` and `||` on all 9 pairs of TRUE, FALSE and NA from comparisons.
